best_for: Hobby and jam developers who want to write 2D games in Lua with a small runtime, and who are fine building menus, editors and tooling themselves.

points.title: Free for commercial games
points.text: LÖVE uses the zlib/libpng license. It costs nothing and you can sell games made with it without paying fees or asking permission.

points.title: A framework, not an editor
points.text: You write Lua code in your own text editor and LÖVE runs it. There is no scene editor or asset browser, so it suits people who like code over visual tools.

points.title: One codebase, five systems
points.text: The project lists Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. Android gets a ready APK, while iOS is offered only as source and libraries, so shipping there means building it yourself in Xcode.

points.title: 11.5 is the stable line
points.text: The current release is 11.5. The `main` branch on GitHub holds the next major version and the project warns it should not be treated as stable, so tutorials and libraries written for 11.x are the safe match.

points.title: macOS: zip download, Homebrew cask off
points.text: The official Mac build is a single zip for macOS 10.11 or later. Homebrew disabled its LÖVE cask on 2026-09-01 because the app fails Apple's Gatekeeper check, so expect a security prompt the first time you open it.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is a community build
points.text: The project's own Linux downloads are an Ubuntu PPA and an x86_64 AppImage. The Flatpak listed here, for x64 and Arm64, is a Flathub build that Flathub does not mark as verified.

points.title: Few old versions here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 3 versions, in 32-bit and 64-bit installers that install for all users. macOS and Linux list only the current release; the project links older builds from its GitHub releases page.
